claims.text_en: BTS Saint Louis (S4, Silom Line) opened 8 February 2021 as Thailand's first infill station built on an already-operating line, elevated over Khlong Sathron where North Sathorn meets South Sathorn Road at the mouth of Soi Sathorn 11 (Saint Louis 3), in front of AIA Tower Sathorn; its footprint straddles khwaeng Silom (Bang Rak district) and khwaeng Yan Nawa (Sathon district). The ~900M THB build was co-funded by the BTS Grow infrastructure fund and the AIA group, which gained a direct connection into AIA Tower. It was renamed from the planned 'Suksawit' to match the Saint Louis neighbourhood and soi.

The 9 most plausibly borrows from the Sathorn/Silom edges of the catchment rather than the Saint Louis sois; no in-soi bar cluster was found.

claims.text_en: Green 7 with a mapped 0.0 ha park is a pure buffer effect: no named public park exists within ~1.3 km of the true station node (OSM query within 1300 m returned none; Lumphini Park's SW corner computes to ~1.38 km NE, the Chaloem Phrakiat 80 Phansa park ~1.7 km S), matching the app's zero. A relocation guide states plainly that Sathorn has 'very little parkland... Lumphini Park is across Rama 4, not inside Sathorn'. The 7 therefore cannot reflect in-unit parkland - likely proximity green/street trees or a catchment-edge effect near the anchor.

preview.text_en: Bangkok's first infill BTS station (2021) dropped into Sathorn's quietest pocket: a Catholic hospital, church and school cluster 200-340 m from the platform, a soi-3 street-food row - and zero mapped parkland.

guide_lead.text_en: Saint Louis is the anti-Chong Nonsi: the Silom line's infill station S4 (opened 8 February 2021) sits where North Sathorn becomes South Sathorn, straddling Bang Rak and Sathon, above a neighbourhood of church, hospital and school rather than towers. Saint Louis Hospital (1898, Thailand's first Catholic hospital) is ~200 m from the platform, the Soi Saint Louis 3 food row supplies B40-70 lunches, and the sois read tree-lined and calm. Two ratings strain against the evidence: nightlife 9 despite guides calling the pocket's scene quiet, and green 7 against a mapped 0.0 ha of park. Note the brief's anchor coordinate sits ~720 m from the real station node and needs re-checking.

strengths.text_en: Hospital-and-church neighbourhood infrastructure at walking distance: Saint Louis Hospital ~200 m from the platform plus schools and a documented multi-faith cluster.
A genuine local food row (St. Louis Soi 3) with long-standing B40-70 vendors, distinct from tourist Silom.

tradeoffs.text_en: Nightlife 9 overstates the pocket: the sources describe a quiet, bar-scarce residential soi, with the nearest real bar clusters one or two stops away.
No park inside the unit - Lumphini is ~1.4 km away across Rama IV - so green 7 rests entirely on buffer effects.

day_night.text_en: Office-clock days (lunch carts, hospital shifts) give way to shophouse-step evenings; the soi goes quiet well before the Sathorn tower bars do.

within_area_variation.text_en: The station frontage on Sathorn Road is office-block territory; one soi south toward Saint Louis Soi 2-3 the character flips to low-rise residential and food carts.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: Sathorn/Silom office workers and hospital-adjacent households who want calm, walkable sois and BTS access without interchange crowds.
Poor fit: nightlife-first renters and park users - both 9s/7s in the scorecard trace to neighbouring units' amenities, not this pocket's.

uncertainties: Anchor mismatch: app anchor '@13.7273-ish' vs OSM station node 13.72082, 100.52669 - >=720 m apart; unit membership near the anchor is unreliable pending coordinator verification (saint-louis-c02).

Rent comparison rests on 2019 listings plus 2026 highlight-level guides; no current portal median for this pocket (saint-louis-c08).
2024-2026 change evidence is thin - a gap, not a verified 'nothing happened'.
